findings.finding: Pricing looks wrong: pricing.mjs sets Haiku at 1/20 of Sonnet on every rate (input 0.1 vs 2, output 0.5 vs 10, cache read 0.01 vs 0.2). That gives -93.9% for +47% tokens. Haiku list prices are closer to 1/3 of Sonnet, which would give about -51%. The threshold for ADOPT is -50%, so the verdict depends on this.
findings.proposedFix: Verify the Haiku rate against the current price table, then recompute A and B per arm and show the per-model rates and token split.

findings.finding: Raw tokens are exactly 2x paired tokens in both arms (878874 = 2 x 439437; 1296790 = 2 x 648395). Likely per-repetition averaging, but not documented; the bad-token rule uses paired, the headline uses raw.
findings.proposedFix: Document the definition and assert it in a unit test.

findings.finding: The cascade was never exercised live: 0 visible-check failures, 0 escalations. Escalation path, its cost accounting and silent-miss detection have no real evidence. Rule-of-three upper bound on Haiku strict-fail is about 25% at 0/12.
findings.proposedFix: Add cases where Haiku fails the visible check, plus a forced-fail control run.

findings.finding: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE stands: the frozen precondition (Haiku passes strict first time on every case) fired, and the token rule (B +47% with no extra passes) also fired. Do not upgrade the verdict.
findings.proposedFix: Keep verdict; record both triggers in deviations.

findings.finding: Offline gate checks routing only for haiku and tests planted bugs written by the author; it does not show that Haiku makes such mistakes.
findings.proposedFix: Build ref/wrong from real failing Haiku outputs in a pilot.

findings.finding: B used more turns (66 vs 47) and tool calls (69 vs 53). Per-run attribution (route call, visible check reruns, wrapper) is not logged, so the cause is unproven.
findings.proposedFix: Log route, visible-check and wrapper turns separately in the driver.
